samples.summary: User-controlled `:tabId` is used directly as an object key and then written into (`ws.images = {}`), so a request with `tabId=__proto__` can reach an assignment onto `Object.prototype` if the root ever behaves like a plain object
samples.evidence: `setImages` takes `:tabId` straight from the URL (Express URL-decodes, so `%5F%5Fproto%5F%5F` → `__proto__`) and does `root.sheets?.[tabId]` in `worksheetOrThrow` (line 51-57). On a plain JS object `sheets['__proto__']` returns `Object.prototype` — truthy — so the NotFound guard passes and `doc.update` then executes `ws.images = {}` followed by `ws.images[image.id] = image` (lines 97-98), writing attacker-controlled data onto `Object.prototype`. Against a real Yorkie object proxy the outcome depends on the SDK's `get` trap (the SDK is not installed in this tree, so I could not confirm which way it falls); the controller's own spec harness uses a plain object, which is the shape where this is exploitable. Note the identical pattern already exists pre-change in `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:106-110`, so this is a new instance of an existing pattern rather than a new class. A cheap fix is to reject any `tabId` that is not present in `root.tabOrder`, or to use `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(sheets, tabId)`.

samples.summary: No maximum length on a comment body: `normalizeBody` accepts any string, so a single authenticated write can push up to the 25MB global body limit into the CRDT, per request, with no cap
samples.evidence: `normalizeBody` only checks `typeof raw === 'string'` and that the trimmed value is non-empty, then returns the body verbatim; `comments.controller.ts` createThread/reply/editComment call it and store the result with no length check. `main.ts:20` sets the body-parser limit to 25MB, and `@Body() body: unknown` has no DTO so the global `ValidationPipe` skips it entirely (no metatype). Any workspace member or write-scoped API key can therefore append ~25MB per request into a Yorkie document, which retains history — an authenticated storage-amplification vector. Contrast the client-reported path, where `CommentNotificationDto` caps `preview` at 2000 and `threadId`/`commentId` at 200. Searched: comments.controller.ts, comment-ops.ts, packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts (`assertNonEmpty`), notification.dto.ts — found no length constraint anywhere on `Comment.body`.

samples.summary: The notification plan is cast `as CommentNotificationDto[]` and passed straight to `NotificationService.createFromComment`, bypassing every class-validator constraint the HTTP notification route relies on (MaxLength on threadId/commentId, ArrayMaxSize on recipients)
samples.evidence: `notify()` does `planCommentNotifications({...}) as CommentNotificationDto[]` and calls `this.notificationService.createFromComment(actorId, plan)` directly, so the `@MaxLength(200)` on `CommentNotificationDto.threadId`/`commentId` and `@ArrayMaxSize(50)` on `recipientUserIds` (notification.dto.ts:41-61) never run. `thread.id` and `comment.id` originate from the Yorkie CRDT, which any collaborator with direct document write access controls, so unbounded strings can reach `prisma.notification.createMany` including the `dedupeKey` column that carries a unique index (`dedupeKeyFor`, notification.service.ts:90-98). Service-side caps (`MAX_RECIPIENTS`, `sanitizePreview`) still hold, so the impact is limited to oversized ids/DB errors, which the controller's try/catch swallows. The docs hunk also records that this path skips `UserThrottlerGuard`; the global IP-keyed `ThrottlerGuard` (app.module.ts:97-104,128) still applies.

samples.summary: `SheetImage.src` is accepted verbatim with no scheme or origin validation, so a write-scoped caller can plant arbitrary external / `data:` URLs into a document that every other viewer's browser then fetches
samples.evidence: `parseImage` validates `src` only with `requireString(i.src, 'src')` — no allowlist of schemes or of the workspace image origin. The stored value is rendered by `image-object-layer.tsx:216` (``) and fetched by `getOrLoadImage`, so a hostile entry causes every viewer of the sheet to issue a request to an attacker host (IP/UA disclosure, open-tracking). The share-token leak variant is already blocked by `isTrustedWorkspaceImageUrl` (packages/frontend/src/api/share-image-url.ts:27-42), and `javascript:`/`data:` in an `` is not script-executable, which is why this is hardening rather than an exploit. That the CLI ships a full SSRF gate for document image URLs (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts) shows these URLs are already treated as untrusted at fetch time. Searched parseImages, the SheetImage type in packages/sheets, and the frontend render path for any scheme check — none exists.

samples.summary: The new author-only edit/delete gate derives its decision from `author.userId` stored inside the CRDT, which is client-written data the same principals can rewrite directly through Yorkie
samples.evidence: `assertCommentAuthor` compares `commentAuthorId(comment)` — a string read out of `sheets[tab].comments[...].comments[].author.userId` — against `String(req.user.id)`. That field is written by whichever client created the comment (the editor's stores, or any party that can attach to the Yorkie document with write access, including share-link editors). Anyone able to write the CRDT directly can therefore set `author.userId` to their own id to gain API delete/edit authority over content they did not write, or to someone else's id to make the API refuse deletes. The gate is still a real improvement for API-only callers (before it, any workspace member could delete anybody's comment), so this is a note on the trust boundary rather than a regression: the check cannot be stronger than the store it reads. I did not confirm whether the Yorkie auth webhook lets a share-link viewer write, hence low confidence.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: worksheet-images.controller.ts:53-60 gates on a bare truthiness check (`root.sheets?.[tabId]`) over an attacker-controlled route param, and lines 106-113 then write `ws.images = {}` / `ws.images[image.id] = image`. Nothing sanitizes `tabId`: the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-66) covers DTO bodies, not raw @Param strings, and none of the three guards inspects tabId. Refutation grounds all fail. `not-present`: verified present. `already-guarded`: the only candidate is the Yorkie SDK get trap, which is not in this tree and which the repo's own docblock (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:88-90) calls "safe only by accident" for `__proto__` — and it explicitly does NOT cover `toString`/`toJSON`/`toJS`/`toJSForTest`/`getID`, which the same docblock (lines 84-88) says the proxy answers with a truthy function that "walked past a bare `if (!worksheet)`". So the Tab-not-found gate is bypassable on a real proxy too, not just on the plain-object spec fixture. `out-of-scope`: a user-controlled key used as an assignment target (prototype pollution / magic-key bypass of a resource gate on a write path) is unsafe input handling, in the security lane. Decisively, this repo already recognized and fixed the identical pattern in worksheet-structure.controller.ts:104-113 using `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(sheets).includes(tabId)`, with dedicated regression tests for `__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, `toJSON`, `toJS`, `toJSForTest`, `getID`; grep shows that helper is used in exactly one file, so the images controller is the unprotected instance.
